Merge Data Frames or Lists by Common Variable(s)

Source: R/merge_by_common.R
merge_by_common.Rd

This function merges two data frames or lists by their common variable(s). It uses find_merge_var to identify the shared columns between the two inputs and performs a full join using dplyr::full_join.

Usage

merge_by_common(x, y = NULL)

Arguments

x

A data frame, or a list of data frames.

y

A data frame (optional). If provided, the function will merge x and y by the common column(s). If y is NULL and x is a list, the elements of x are merged in order, each on the columns it shares with the result so far.

Value

A single data frame, the full join of the inputs.

See also

full_join, find_merge_var()

Examples

# Example 1: Merging two data frames with a common column
df1 <- data.frame(ID = 1:3, Value = c(10, 20, 30))
df2 <- data.frame(ID = c(2, 3, 4), Value = c(200, 300, 400))
merged_df <- merge_by_common(df1, df2)

# Example 2: Merging a list of data frames by common columns
list_df <- list(
    data.frame(ID = 1:3, Value = c(10, 20, 30)),
    data.frame(ID = c(2, 3, 4), Value = c(200, 300, 400))
)
merged_list <- merge_by_common(list_df)
